name: Sara Kaba
sweep_summary: Sara Kaba [sbz] is not in the catalog. The single stress/prosody-titled bibliography item (Bardiaux 2013, regional prosodic indices in Belgian French) is a Glottolog machine misattribution — its record says lgcode 'Sara Kaba [sbz] (computerized assignment from \"perceptive\")' with language of publication French — so it is irrelevant (other-language-or-variety, priority none). Pulling all 23 Glottolog records attached to sara1319 (saved as glottolog_sara1319_biblist.bib) shows 11 of them are the same kind of keyword noise ('perceptive', 'kabba'); the genuinely language-specific entries are Fédry, Danay & Ma... 1981 'Initiation à la langue kaba (kyabé)' (CCL Sarh, print only — the best lead for a phonology statement on sbz, not obtained), Palayer & Solekaye 2004 'Dictionnaire démé' (sister language Kaba Deme), Moser's Kabba papers (Kabba is more likely Kaba [ksp] of Paoua than sbz), a 1935 wordlist, a 1931 melody sample and sociolinguistic surveys. Beyond the item list, I fetched sources Keegan's open Sara-Bagirmi Project PDFs: the Kaba Na dictionary with English introduction (sister language kwv) states three level tones (high, mid, low) with tonal-change processes and never mentions stress; Keegan's Sara transcription note likewise gives three even tones for the Sara languages. No first-hand stress statement for sbz itself exists in anything read; best_new_statement found=false. Semantic Scholar/OpenAlex APIs and HathiTrust refused, archive.org search returned nothing.
